title: The whole day
hookLine: a day lived with Allah from waking to sleep
tomorrow: one day a week gets a bath and perfume first. which one, and why?

cards: The chairs go up on the tables, the espresso machine ticks as it cools, and Dadi, who came by for a ride home, asks Amira a question from the corner booth: so, what are you keeping from these two weeks?
It's a good question for anyone at the end of a stretch. The tradition's answer covers the whole day, and it starts and ends with two short lines.

teach.h: IN YOUR NAME I DIE AND I LIVE.
teach.b: In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ, lying down at night, would say: in Your name, O God, I die and I live. And waking: praise be to God, who gave us life after He had made us die, and to Him is the return.
Sleep as a small death, waking as a small rising. Everything else in the day sits between those two lines, and the last fourteen days filled it in.
Five posts, fifty become five: the day has a frame. Fajr, said to the pillow. The morning adhkar, on the porch or on the bus.
Dhuhr in the rush, 'Asr in the slide, Maghrib at a door other families stand at too, 'Isha and then the lamp.
Between the posts: a portion read, a little given, a smile on no sleep, ten minutes learned, and the day counted before bed. None of it is big.
That's the point of a daily rhythm: a whole day lived with God isn't a day of nothing but prayer.
It's an ordinary day, from waking to sleep, with God named at both ends and five times between.

how: Muslims say short remembrances on waking and before sleeping, from the hadith; together with the five prayers, the morning and evening adhkar, a daily portion of Qur'an and small acts of charity, they make up a day's ordinary rhythm.

o: an ordinary day lived with God from waking until sleep
a day set apart each year for fasting and prayer only
the hours between Fajr and sunrise, kept for worship

games.q: the whole day — tap the pairs.
p: in Your name I die and I live
life after He made us die
a portion, a gift, a kindness

s: a day lived with God means a day of nothing but prayer
it's an ordinary day, with God named at both ends and five times between.
the Prophet had a short line for lying down and another for waking
in Sahih al-Bukhari: in Your name I die and I live; and praise for life after a small death.

games.q: a coworker sees you pray in the back of the shop and asks, 'isn't it hard to fit all that into a day?' what's the truest answer?
o: 'honestly, on busy days most of it gets skipped.'
'it's only hard if your faith isn't strong enough.'
'it's less fitting it in than building around it.'
games.why: the five posts go in first and the day is built between them, from waking to sleep. that's the whole two weeks in a sentence.

practice: Stand up and walk slowly across the room and back, about a minute, as if you were walking the day from its first step to its last. Then sit for the rest of the time, the walk finished, and let the room settle around you.

wordCard.voice: The whole day: a day lived with God from waking to sleep, opened and closed with two short lines, with five prayers and small good things between.

orig.note: Arabic: in Your name, O God, I die and I live; said on lying down (Bukhari 6312).

carryVoice: Last line of the daily rhythm: from waking to sleep, the whole of it named. Fourteen days, one frame.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 6312 (on lying down: in Your name, O God, I die and I live; on waking: praise be to God who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the return)
Qur'an 39:42 (God takes the souls at death, and those that have not died in their sleep)
